Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A.Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA corner Mapaguuahal St., Diliman, Quezon City Telephone 925.1 1.48 • 925.SS.SS • 925.03.32 www.dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNOERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG Legal Opinion No. 23, S. 2013 HON. DANILO O. LEYBLE 20 JUN 2013 City Mayor Antipolo, Rizal Dear Mayor Leyble, This pertains to your letter & ted 21 May 2013 requesting this Department's opinion regarding Resolution Numbers 1 19 and 120 of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal which declared City Resolution No. 2013-013 (Annual Investment Plan) and City Appropriation Ordinance No. 2013-001 (Annual Budget) as "invalid and inoperative" on the sole ground that only eight (8) members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo City approved and enacted the said measures last 29 April 2013. Per your letter and its attachments, you filed a Petition for Mandamus against the members of the Sangguniang Pallungsod of Antipolo City before the Regional Trial Court (RTC), Branch 74 of Antipolo City, seeking judicial relief för the continued failure and/or refusal of the Sangguniang Panlungsod to enact and approve the 2013 Annual Investment Plan and the Annual Budget for 2013 of Antipolo City. In an Order dated 25 April 2013, the RTC granted the petition, and directed the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo to "convene and hold session as a collegial body exclusively for the deliberation of the 2013 Annual Investment Plan and the Annual Budget for 2013 of Antipolo Chy, until the same are respectively approved and passed. ' Accordingly, in a letter dated 2S April 2013, you wrote Hon. Susana G. Say, Antipolo City Vice Mayor and Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, informing the latter of the aforesaid Order of the RTC and enjoining the sanggunian to comply with the same. In compliance with the aforementioned RTC Order and directive from your office, eight (8) members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo City held a regular session on 29 April 2013. Despite due notice, ten (IO) members of the sanggunian were allegedly absent in the said session, in which City Resolution No. 2013-013 and City Appropriation Ordinance No. 2013-001 were enacted and approved. On 07 May 2013, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal, pursuant to its review power under the Local Government Code of 1991 (Code), enacted Resolution Nos. 119 and 120 declaring the aforementioned measures as invalid and inoperative for having been enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo City without the requisite quorum as provided under Section 53 of the same Code. Hence, your queries, which are hereto quoted, viz:

I. Is Lhe declaration by Llte Sangguniang Panlalawigan pursuant to its review power on City ResolutÄ)T1 No. 2013-013 and Appropriation Ordinance No. 2013-001 as both "invalid and inoperative" on the sole ground that only eight (8) members out of eighteen (18) members of Sangguniang Panlungsod approved the subject resolution and ordinance, a valid (sic) legislative act? 2. Does the Sangguniang Panlalawigan has (sic) the power to declare such ordinance and resolution as invalid and inoperative other Lhan the ground of ultra vires? Before dwelling on your queries, may we note that based on the facts and circumstances you stated in your letter-request, it appears that what are at issue are the validity of City Resolution No. 2013-013 and Appropriation Ordinance No. 2013-001, purportedly enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo and Resolution Nos. 119 and 120 purportedly enacted by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal. Legislative acts enjoy the presumption of validity, and legislative bodies are presumed to have carried out their function regularly in enacting the said measures, pursuant to Rule 131, Section 3 (m) of the Rules of Couil. Generally, therefore, the matter of the validity of legislative enactments may appropriately be threshed out in the proper judicial proceeding, as only courts are empowered by law to finally determine the validity of Ihe herein questioned measures and their compliance with Lhe provisions of the Constitucion, the Code and pertinent laws. Be that as it may, we shall render an opinion on the issues herein raised solely for purposes of academic discussion, considering that this Department previously had the occasion to discourse on the said matters. In reply to your first query. it is our view that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal erred in disapproving City Resolution No. 2013-013 and City Appropriation Ordinance No. 2013- 001 on the sole ground that saud measures were approved by only eight (8) out of the eighteen (18) members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo City. Please be advised that this Depart ment already had the occasion to elucidate on the extent of the review power of the sangguniang panlalawigan over a city's appropriations ordinance in DILG Legal Opinion NO. 102, S. 2004 (copy attached). Quoting Section 3271 of the Code; the aforementioned Legal Opinion held that the extent of the review power of the sangguniang panlalawigan over a city's appropriations Section 327. Review of Appropri,rion Ordinances of Component Cities and Municipalities.- The Saogguniang Panlalawigan shall review the ordinance authorizing annual or supplemental appropriations of component cities and municipalities in same manner and within the same period prescribed for the review of other ordinances. xxx If within the same period, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall have ascertained that

ordinance extends only as fal as looking into whether or not a city's appropriations ordinance complies with the requirements and limitations set forth under Title V, Book II of the Local Government Code, or the title being referred to in the aforementioned Section. Applying the aforesaid principle to your query, the review of City Resolution No. 2013- 013 and City Appropriation Ordinance No. 2013-001 by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal should have been confined to the determination of said measures' compliance with the budgetary requirements laid down in Sections 324 and 325 of the LGC, viz: "SECTION 324. Budgeta1Y Requirements. The budget of local government units for any fiscal year shall comply with the following requirements: a. The aggregate anlount appropriated shall not exceed the estimates of mcome; b. Full provision Ghall be made for al statutory and contractual obligations of [he local government unit concerned: Provided, however, That the a mount of appropriations for debt servicing shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the regular income of the local government unit concerned; c. In case of provinces, cities, and municipalities, aid to component barangays shall be provided in amounts of not less than One Thousand (Pl Pesos per barangay, and; d. Five percent (5%) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as an annual lump appropriation for unforeseen expenditures arising from the occurrence of calamities: Provided, however, That such appropriation shall be used only in the area, or a portion thereof, of Lhe local government unit or other areas declared in a state of calamity by the President." (Note: See RA 8185 for amendment of par. "SECTION 325. General Limitations. - The use of the provincial, city, and municipal funds shall be subject to the following limitations: a) The total appropriations, whether annual or supplemental, for personal services of local government unit for one (I) fiscal year shall not exceed forty-five percent (45%) in the case of first to third class provinces, cities and municipalities, and fifty-five percent (55%) in the case of fourth class or lower, of the total annual income from regular sources realized in he next preceding fiscal year. The appropriations requirements set forth in this the sangguniang panlalawigan shall, within the ninety-day period hereinabove prescribed. declare such ordinance inoperative in its entirety or in part. Items of appropriations contrary to limitations prescribed herein shall be disallowed or reduced accordingly. xxx" (underscoring supplied).

for salaries, wages, representation and transportation allowances of officials and employees of the public utilities and economic enterprises owned, operated, and maintained by the local government unit concerned shall not be included in the annual budget or in the computation of the maximum amount for personal services. 'The appropriations for the personal services of such enterprises shall be charged to their resvective budgets; b) No official or employee shall be entitled to a salary rate higher than the maximum fixed for his position or other positions of equivalent rank by applicable laws or rules and regulations issued thereunder; c) No local fund shall be appropriated to increase or adjust salaries or wages of officials and employees of the national government, except as may be expressly authorized by law; d) In cases of abolition of positions and the creation of new ones resulting from the abolition of existing positions in the career service, such abolition or creation shall be made in accordance with pertinent provisions of this code and the civil service law, rules and regulations; e) Positions in the official plantilla for career positions which are occupied by incumbents holding permanent appointments shall be covered by adequate appropriations; f) No changes in designation or nomenclature of positions resulting in a promotion or demotion in rank or increase in compensation shall be allowed, except when the position is actually vacant, and the filling of such positions shall be strictly made in accordance with the civil service law, rules and regulations; g) The creation of new positions and salary increases or adjustments shall in no case be made retroactive; and h) The annual appropriations for discretionary purposes of the local chief executive shall not exceed two percent (2%) of the actual receipts derived from basic real property tax in the next preceding calendar year. Discretionary funds shall be disbursed only for public purposes to be supported by appropriate vouchers and subject to such guidelines as may be prescribed by law. No amount shall be appropriated for Lhe same purpose except as authorized under this Section.' Coming now to your second query, aside from the fact that the sangguniang panlalawigan is bound to limit its review of appropriations ordinance to the requirements set forth by the aforementioned provisions of the Code, Section 56 (c) thereof is clear in providing for the only ground upon which a city ordinance or resolution may be declared invalid by the sangguniang panlalawigann i.e., the ordinance is beyond the power conferred upon the sanggunian concerned.

In relation thereto, the case of Moday vs. CA (G.R. No. 107916, February 20, 1997) is instructive. In the said case, the Supreme Court, citing Velazco vs. Blas (G.R. No. L- 30456, July 30, 1982) lulled that: "The only ground upon which a provincial board may declare any municipal resolution, coulinance, or order invalid is when such resolution, ordinance or order is 'beyond the power conferred upon the council or president making the sane.' Absolutely no other ground is recognized by the law. A strictly legal question is before the provincial board in its consideration of a munieipal resolution, ordinance or order. The provincial (board's) disapproval Of any resolution. ordinance or order must be premised specifically upon the fact that such resolution, ordinance, or order is outside the sc:tpe of the legal powers conferred by law. If a provincial board passes these limits, it usurps the legislative functions of the municipal council, or president. Such has been the consistent course of executive authority." (Emphasis supplied) It is to be noted that the reason given by the Sangguniang Pawlalawigan of Rizal in disapproving the Annual Plan ancl Appropriations Ordinance of Antipolo City is the alleged enactment of the measures in question by only eight (8) of the eighteen (18) members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Antipolo City, in a regular session claimed to have been conducted without the requisite quorum. To our mind, the reason given is not supported by the provisions of the Local Government Code and jurispluclence as cited above since the review authority of the sangguniang panlalawigan does not encompass questions on quorum. Therefore, we are of the ovinion that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Rizal has exceeded its review mandate vis-å-vis your city's Annual Investment Plan and Annual Budget for the calendar year 2013. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary
